analysis: Only head text of docs/developer/build.md was supplied (no diff), so I could not isolate the changed lines. I read it for security-relevant claims. Line 249: official-build registration via scoped POST /v1/releases with no per-release hardware qualification or manual approval. Lines 251-255: secret-bearing release jobs run on signed annotated tags in master ancestry, or trusted master, without environment approval attachments, and assume trusted repository writers. Line 327 says protected signing and publication jobs keep their existing approvals, which is inconsistent with line 254. The canonical model (A-017, T-054) requires independent operator approval of the exact CodeDirectory and says CI release keys cannot grant approval. This is flagged as a threat-model/doc reconciliation gap. Other content is CI cache, test and tooling description. The cache statements (unsigned products only, no signing keys, content-verified mtimes, discarded runtime resources) look benign. The Homebrew installer is pinned by SHA-256 and the gh CLI archive is checksum-verified. Later passes should check release-swift.yml, provider-release-publication.py and the coordinator release handler to confirm whether registration can grant App Attest build qualification without the independent operator approval.

findings.detail: docs/developer/build.md line 249 says release publication registers the exact official build through POST /v1/releases and that 'No per-release hardware qualification or manual approval is required'. Lines 251-255 add that secret-bearing release jobs use repository-scoped secrets without environment approval attachments and assume trusted repository writers. The canonical threat model (A-017, T-054) says an independently authenticated operator approves the exact signed binary and full CodeDirectory, and that CI release keys cannot grant approval. If this describes real behaviour, a compromised or abused CI release path or tag/master writer could mint App Attest serving-eligible builds without independent approval. That would weaken T-054 and A-017, and could let an unqualified or malicious provider build obtain serving authorization (T-052). If it does not, the doc misstates the trust model. The PR should either update T-054, A-017, A-011 and TB-011 to state what 'official build' registration authorizes versus App Attest qualification, or fix the text. It should also reconcile the 'no environment approval' statement at line 254 with line 327 ('retain their existing approvals'). I could not confirm the changed behaviour because only the file's head text was supplied.
findings.title: Docs describe official-build registration without per-release approval, conflicting with the threat model's independent build-qualification control
